title.narrative: Lifesaving health responses at Ofla, Korem, Zata and Chercher woredas

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtMedical Teams International is applying for the 3rd Reserve Allocation Strategy 2024 to deliver essential, life-saving health support in the contested areas regions as that of Ofla, Korem, Chercher, and Zata woredas. In August 2024, the MIRA assessment focused on evaluating the operating environment, the conditions in return areas, and the immediate needs of IDP returnees and existing populations in contested areas covering Alamata, Korem towns, and woredas such as Raya Alamata, Zata, Ofla/Wofla, and Chercher was conducted by Aid workers. the assessment identified 50,153 returnees with significant humanitarian needs, including food, shelter, health services, WaSH, cash support, livelihood recovery, HLP services, and protection for both returnees and host communities. Additionally, Tigray Region plans to return 52,000 IDPs to Alamata and Korem towns and surrounding rural districts (Raya Alamata, Zata, Ofla/Wofla, and Chercher). By the time of the assessment, the government had already returned approximately 25,000 IDPs to Alamata Town and Raya Alamata. There were 25,000 spontaneous returns, 25,153 Organized returns, totaling 50,153 returnees in Alamata and Korem towns, and Raya Alamata, Zata, Ofla/Wofla, and Chercher woredas These groups of IDPs predominantly reside with host communities and have dire humanitarian needs due to a lack of humanitarian assistance and access to essential services. ltbrgtThrough health interventions, MTI aims to reach approximately 82,000 (50,153 Returnees and IDPs) beneficiaries by offering free and comprehensive primary healthcare services. The MTI Team Lead conducts technical support visits and provides on-the-job training in the health centers (HC) on a weekly basis. Health facility service quality is monitored on a quarterly basis with the MTI Abbreviated Balanced Card tool. MTI will deploy 4 MHT teams composed of a medical officer, psychiatric nurse, nurse, midwifery, and community mobilizers at the four woredas, namely Ofla, Korem, Chercher, and Zata woredas. The MHT teams will focus on maternal and child health, enhancing routine and emergency immunization efforts, and supporting disease surveillance with adequate supplies and equipment. Services will include integrated comprehensive MHPSS, family planning counseling, ANC, PNC, syndromic treatment of STIs, and CMR/IPV. MTI will also support the functionalization of 5 government health facilities (Bala, Maymaedo, Sessela, Zata, and Korem health centers), and support Korem General Hospital with essential medicines and medical supplies. Furthermore, MTI will support 13 health centers with public health activities, including health promotion, disease prevention campaigns, immunization drives, and strengthening routine health services. These efforts will be complemented by disease surveillance and capacity-building training for government workers who have not received continuing education or training during the recent conflict. The training will cover critical areas such as BEmONC, PHEM, PSCM, mhGAP-HIG, and PSEA, aiming to enhance the ability of government clinicians to effectively address community health needs. MTI will request IAHK and RH kits from WHO for the MHTs, and UNFPA to support HFs respectively. ltbrgtlt/pgt
